chat.title: AI chat
chat.description: Built-in conversational assistant, backed by the MCP server tools: it only sees what the user is allowed to see.
chat.enable: Enable the AI chat for the whole instance
chat.note: When unticked, the assistant disappears from the menu and the sphere is no longer offered, for everyone. Individual access is set by role: “Use the AI assistant” (read) and “Allow changes by the AI assistant” (write, always subject to the user’s confirmation).

apiKey.label: OpenRouter API key
apiKey.help: The chat goes through OpenRouter only: routing, privacy and PDF reading depend on it. Recommended: set OPENROUTER_API_KEY in the .env file (the database stores it in plain text).

chat.dictation: Voice dictation (Whisper, local transcription; the model is downloaded from HuggingFace)

widget.title: Floating assistant
widget.description: The sphere at the bottom right of every screen: the same chat, in a panel, whose tools follow the open page.
widget.enable: Offer the floating assistant on every page
widget.closable: Let the user hide the sphere, until the page is next loaded
widget.note: The sphere only appears to people with access to the AI chat: chat enabled above, and a role that grants it. Hiding the sphere is not stored anywhere: it comes back when the page is reloaded.

privacy.title: Privacy and routing
privacy.description: OpenRouter-specific options: they decide who processes your exchanges and what they may keep.

dataCollection.label: Data collection
dataCollection.deny: Denied - providers that do not train on your data
dataCollection.help: Denied by default: providers that retain exchanges are excluded from routing.

zdr.label: Zero data retention (ZDR)
zdr.help: Only uses endpoints that retain no prompt. This is the strongest guarantee offered by OpenRouter; it narrows the choice of providers and may exclude some models.

privacy.nitro: Nitro routing - favours the fastest providers, often at a higher cost

generation.title: Generation
generation.description: These settings affect the length of replies and the reasoning time, and therefore the cost of each exchange.

reasoning.label: Default reasoning

options.low: Short - a minimal amount of analysis
options.medium: Medium - a balance between accuracy and speed

reasoning.help: Before replying, some models reason separately: the higher the level, the more reliable the reply on a calculation or a variance to explain, and the slower and more expensive it is - reasoning tokens are billed. Users can change this level in the chat; a model that cannot reason simply ignores the setting.

maxTokens.label: Maximum length of a reply
maxTokens.help: In tokens - about three quarters of a word each. 8,192 is a very long reply; it is a safety ceiling, not a target. It does not limit the conversation, only each reply.

temperature.label: Temperature
temperature.help: The model’s freedom, from 0 to 2. Low, it stays factual and reproducible; high, it becomes inventive. On planning data, 0.3 is a good compromise - avoid going higher.

maxDuration.label: Maximum duration of a reply (minutes)
maxDuration.help: From 1 to 30 minutes. A reply continues and finishes on the server even if the user leaves the page; past this limit, it is interrupted and what has been written is kept.

concurrent.label: Simultaneous replies per user
concurrent.help: From 1 to 20, across all conversations. Beyond that, a new question is refused until a reply has finished or been stopped. A conversation never has more than one reply in progress at a time.

prompt.title: System prompt
prompt.description: It keeps the assistant within the scope of the planning: outside your data, it refuses. Written in English; the assistant replies in the user’s language.
prompt.resetTooltip: Revert to the original prompt (remember to save)
prompt.help: is replaced by the application title. The typography rule (no em dash) is always added, even with a custom prompt.

quotas.title: AI chat quotas
quotas.description: Monthly cap per person, measured on the actual cost of replies, shared by the Assistant page and the floating assistant. Users only see a gauge, never an amount.
quotas.resetOneTooltip: Reset: sets this account’s usage back to zero

settings.title: Settings
settings.period: Current period since {start} · next reset on {next}.

amount.label: Monthly amount per person
amount.help: In dollars, as OpenRouter bills. 0 lifts the quota for everyone.

resetDay.label: Reset day
resetDay.help: From the 1st to the 28th of the month, at midnight (instance time zone): that way the day exists every month.

resetAll.label: Reset for everyone
resetAll.tooltip: Starts again from zero for every account, without waiting for the reset day

confirmResetAll.title: Reset everyone’s quotas?
confirmResetAll.description: Every account’s usage starts again from zero right now, whatever the reset day. Replies in progress run to completion. The operation is recorded in the log.

confirmResetOne.title: Reset this account’s quota?
confirmResetOne.description: The usage of {name} starts again from zero right now. The operation is recorded in the log.
